Q: What is a Windows workgroup best described as?
Option1: A peer-to-peer grouping where each computer manages its own users and shares
Option2: A centralized directory service with domain controllers
Option3: A cloud-only identity service that replaces local accounts
Option4: A hidden wireless network profile

Q: What is a Windows domain best described as?
Option1: A centralized directory where accounts, policies, and resources are managed by domain controllers
Option2: A temporary ad hoc group for file sharing
Option3: A single computer with multiple local users
Option4: A guest wireless portal

Q: What are shared resources in Windows?
Option1: Folders, printers, or devices made available over the network with permissions
Option2: Only printers attached by USB
Option3: Files that are copied locally by default
Option4: Applications installed for all users

Q: What is a mapped drive in File Explorer?
Option1: A drive letter that points to a network shared folder using a UNC path
Option2: A virtual disk created from RAM
Option3: A compressed archive mounted as a folder
Option4: A local partition that hides system files

Q: What role does a file server provide?
Option1: Centralized storage and sharing of files with permissions and quotas
Option2: Automatic IP addressing to clients
Option3: Filtering of web requests and content
Option4: Wireless authentication for client devices

Q: What is a firewall exception?
Option1: A rule that allows specific traffic through Windows Defender Firewall
Option2: A rule that blocks all outbound traffic
Option3: A scheduled task that installs updates
Option4: A backup of the firewall configuration

Q: In a firewall rule, what do application restrictions control?
Option1: Which executable file may send or receive specific traffic
Option2: How large a file download may be
Option3: Which user accounts can sign in
Option4: When the computer can go to sleep

Q: What is an IP addressing scheme on a client?
Option1: The plan for static or dynamic addresses, subnet masks, gateways, and ranges
Option2: The list of approved wireless networks
Option3: The naming rules for computer hostnames
Option4: The order in which updates install

Q: What are DNS settings used for on a client?
Option1: Resolving hostnames to IP addresses using configured servers
Option2: Encrypting web traffic end to end
Option3: Advertising the computer to nearby devices
Option4: Balancing traffic across multiple links

Q: What does the subnet mask determine?
Option1: Which portion of an address is the network and which is the host
Option2: Which server performs name resolution
Option3: Which wireless band is used
Option4: Which process may open a port

Q: What is the default gateway used for?
Option1: Forwarding traffic from the local network to other networks such as the internet
Option2: Translating names into addresses
Option3: Isolating wireless guests from internal devices
Option4: Caching frequently used files

Q: What is the key difference between static and dynamic IP on Windows?
Option1: Static is manually configured and does not change; dynamic is assigned automatically and may change
Option2: Static rotates on each restart; dynamic never changes
Option3: Static is wireless only; dynamic is wired only
Option4: Static is for servers only; dynamic is illegal on laptops

Q: What is a VPN connection on Windows?
Option1: An encrypted tunnel over an untrusted network to a private network
Option2: A proxy that rewrites web headers without encryption
Option3: A second wireless card used for guests
Option4: A feature that disables local printing

Q: What is WWAN connectivity?
Option1: Cellular data such as LTE through a mobile broadband adapter
Option2: A short range Bluetooth link
Option3: A wired Ethernet uplink to a router
Option4: A mesh of access points inside one building

Q: What do Windows proxy settings do?
Option1: Direct web requests through an intermediary server, optionally with an automatic configuration script
Option2: Force all applications to use a VPN
Option3: Assign IP addresses to clients
Option4: Select the best wireless channel automatically

Q: What is the difference between Public and Private network profiles?
Option1: Private enables device discovery and file sharing by default; Public is more restrictive for untrusted networks
Option2: Public allows Remote Desktop and Private blocks it
Option3: Public uses static addressing and Private uses dynamic
Option4: Private disables the firewall and Public enables it

Q: Which is a valid UNC path to a share named Docs on server FS1?
Option1: \\\\FS1\\\\Docs
Option2: C:\\Docs
Option3: http://FS1/Docs
Option4: FS1:Docs

Q: What is a metered connection in Windows?
Option1: A network marked to limit background data usage such as updates and sync
Option2: A secure tunnel that encrypts all traffic
Option3: A wireless network that hides its SSID
Option4: A power plan that limits CPU usage

Q: Which behavior is most likely on a metered connection by default?
Option1: Deferring large updates and pausing some cloud sync activity
Option2: Blocking all incoming connections regardless of rules
Option3: Disabling the wired adapter automatically
Option4: Forcing all traffic through a proxy

Q: You must access a corporate share over the internet. What should you do first?
Option1: Create a VPN connection, then map the drive with a UNC path
Option2: Change the network profile to Public and browse the share directly
Option3: Set the connection to metered and email files
Option4: Create a proxy rule pointing to the file server

Q: A user can reach sites by IP numbers but not by names. What setting is most likely wrong?
Option1: DNS server addresses
Option2: Default gateway address
Option3: Subnet mask length
Option4: Metered connection flag

Q: A desktop has a valid IP and mask but cannot reach the internet. What is most likely wrong?
Option1: Default gateway address
Option2: Computer name
Option3: Time zone
Option4: Wallpaper theme

Q: Where do you change Public vs Private for a connected network?
Option1: Settings > Network & Internet > Wi-Fi or Ethernet > Network profile
Option2: Control Panel > Administrative Tools > Services
Option3: Task Manager > Performance
Option4: Device Manager > Network adapters

Q: Where do you configure manual proxy or automatic script?
Option1: Settings > Network & Internet > Proxy
Option2: Control Panel > System
Option3: Settings > Accounts > Sign-in options
Option4: File Explorer > Options

Q: What is the first step to map a network drive?
Option1: Right-click This PC and choose Map network drive
Option2: Open Device Manager and add legacy hardware
Option3: Open Services and start the Workstation service
Option4: Create a new local user account

Q: How do you share a locally attached printer with another Windows computer?
Option1: Share the printer from Printers & Scanners and connect using its shared name
Option2: Turn on Internet Connection Sharing for the printer
Option3: Add the printer to the proxy list
Option4: Switch the network profile to Public
